title: Dyno Training
texts: Practice dynos by removing holds from easier climbs

CAUTION:  Dyno training can be risky and should only be completed by healthy athletes after a thorough warm-up.  Ensure that you are well versed in and practice proper falling techniques.  Ensure to only perform dynos from heights you are comfortable with and can safely fall from.

Begin by finding a boulder between V0 and V4 (5A - 6B+).  Identify holds on the boulder that can be skipped by dynoing.  The gaps between the moves should be large enough that you need to jump between the holds.  After completing the boulder once, rest for 2 minutes, remove additional holds, and repeat the climb.  The climb should get progressively harder as you remove holds and the dynos become larger.  A good difficulty level is completing the boulder on your first 2 or 3 repeats, but by the 4th repetition, the dyno should be challenging to complete.

Once you can no longer complete the boulder, rest for 5 minutes before repeating the same process on 2 additional boulders.  This workout should be performed on various wall angles ranging from slab to very steep.  You should plan to perform approximately 4 reps on 3 different boulders for a total of 12 dynos of varying degrees of difficulty.
